jobs.description:
Job Description

Director, Enterprise Applications

Office of the Chief Information Officer, Corporate Services

Status:
Regular Full Time

Hiring Range: $162,893 - $183,255
p er annum (plus comprehensive benefits )

Work Mode: Hybrid* see below for more details about this work mode.

Location: 10 Peel Centre Drive, Brampton ON ( Google Maps)

Hours of work: 35 hours per week

Be bold. Think bigger. Create lasting impact.

At Peel Region, technology enables the essential public services our communities rely on every day.

Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director, Enterprise Applications
will shape Peel’s enterprise technology direction and lead the modernization and sustainable operation of critical platforms, including SAP S/4HANA, SAP Concur and IBM Maximo Enterprise Asset Management.

This is an opportunity to lead meaningful business transformation and strengthen systems supporting approximately 7,000 users across Peel Region.

The opportunity

You will connect technology investments with Peel’s strategic priorities, service outcomes and future needs. Working with senior leaders, business teams and external partners, you will lead enterprise application strategy, major implementations, governance, operational sustainment and organizational adoption.

Your leadership will ensure Peel’s enterprise applications are integrated, reliable and positioned to deliver lasting value for employees, services and the community.

Advancing Peel’s strategic priorities

Peel’s Strategic Plan Sets The Direction For Building a Community For Life
. This Role Will Contribute Particularly To Service Excellence, Our People And Future Ready
By:

Modernizing the systems that enable essential public services.
Improving the technology experience for employees and leaders.
Strengthening data, reporting and enterprise decision-making.
Establishing sustainable application support and governance models.
Supporting responsible stewardship of public resources.
Helping employees successfully adopt new technology and ways of working.

Learn more about the Peel Region Strategic Plan .

What You Will Do

Lead Peel’s Enterprise Applications Strategy and Roadmap.
Provide strategic leadership for SAP S/4HANA, SAP Concur, IBM Maximo and other critical enterprise applications.
Oversee complex implementation, modernization, integration and sustainment initiatives.
Align technology investments with service priorities, user needs and measurable organizational benefits.
Establish governance, service standards, service-level agreements and sustainable support models.
Maintain stable operations while leading the transition to modern solutions.
Lead organizational change through stakeholder engagement, business readiness, communications, training and adoption.
Manage procurement, implementation partners, strategic suppliers, contracts, budgets, deliverables and vendor performance.
Identify enterprise risks, resolve complex issues and provide clear advice to senior leaders.
Build trusted relationships across business and technology functions.
Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team that values accountability, collaboration and professional growth.

What You Bring

A relevant postgraduate degree, preferably in Business, Computer Science, Information Technology or a related discipline.
SAP Certified Application Associate and/or SAP Certified Development Associate certification.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
At least eight years of experience implementing enterprise applications in a complex public-sector environment.
A satisfactory Level 2 Criminal Record Check obtained directly from a police station (third-party background checks will not be accepted).
Implementation and operational experience with SAP S/4HANA and SAP Concur and/or IBM Maximo Enterprise Asset Management.
Experience leading large-scale technology implementations across multiple business functions and stakeholder groups.
Strong knowledge and practical application of formal project management methodologies.
Experience managing procurement, implementation partners, contracts, budgets, deliverables and vendor performance.
Experience establishing governance, service standards, service-level agreements and operational support models.
Strong strategic thinking, change leadership, risk management and relationship-building skills.
An understanding of government structures, political considerations and Council-level accountability.

How You Will Demonstrate Peel’s Values

Inclusion: Engage diverse perspectives to create accessible, user-centred enterprise solutions.
Transparency: Establish clear governance and communicate openly about decisions, progress, risks, costs and results.
Care and Support: Lead change with empathy and help employees confidently adopt new technology.
Collaboration: Bring business, technology and external partners together around shared outcomes.
Leadership: Set a clear direction, make accountable decisions, develop people and champion innovation and continuous improvement.

Why work at Peel?

At Peel, you can lead, impact and grow
while helping shape better communities and build a Community for Life
.

You Will Join An Inclusive And Values-led Organization Where Employees Are Encouraged To Be Bold, Think Bigger And Contribute Meaningfully. In This Role, You Will Have The Opportunity To:

Shape Peel’s enterprise applications strategy and future technology roadmap.
Lead transformation across critical business platforms.
Influence decisions that strengthen services and organizational performance.
Improve the technology experience for employees and leaders.
Develop people and build future organizational capability.
Make a lasting contribution to responsive and sustainable public service.

The Peel Employee Experience

As an eligible employee, you will receive:

Comprehensive health, dental and vision benefits, including psychological health supports, effective on your first day.
Automatic enrolment in the OMERS pension plan.
Five weeks of annual vacation accrued monthly.
Three paid personal days, in addition to floating holidays.
Flexible work hours that support well-being and work-life integration.
An inclusive workplace culture grounded in collaborative leadership and meaningful public service.

Join us.

Enterprise applications are more than technology platforms. They enable our employees, strengthen public services and help Peel respond to changing community needs.

Bring your experience, perspective and leadership to Peel and help shape the future of technology-enabled public service.

In this role, you’ll benefit from the flexibility of a hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes meaningful in-person connection. A minimum of two days per week on-site
is expected, with additional in-person presence as operational needs evolve. This arrangement allows for a blend of in person and hybrid work that adapts to support both organizational priorities and employee flexibility and is subject to change over time.

It's important to note that your off-site work location must be within the province of Ontario. This ensures that we're compliant with all regulations and policies.

The Region of Peel offers job based flexible hours of work that allows employees to manage personal and professional responsibilities while at the same time ensures business operational needs and customer service expectations are achieved.

Be bold. Think bigger. Create lasting impact.

About Us

Peel Region consists of the cities of Brampton and Mississauga, and the town of Caledon. Peel Region delivers essential services to more than 1.5 million residents and approximately 200,000 businesses.

We’re working to create a community that is safe, inclusive, and accessible. A place where everyone feels they belong and can access the services they need to thrive throughout each stage of life.

Our workforce is 6,700 strong and s ince 1974, we’ve been delivering a wide range of resident focused services. Our services include paramedic services, health programs, long-term care and services for seniors, child care support, garbage collection and recycling, waste water and water treatment, road maintenance, financial assistance, and housing support.

Recognized by Canada's Healthy Workplace Month® with the Great Employer Award
presented by Excellence Canada, Peel Region is a place where everyone feels they belong. We strive to develop a workplace that values and respects diversity, practices inclusion, recognizes the unique contributions and abilities of all people and facilitates innovative thinking. At Peel Region, people come first. Each employee has an important role within our community and when we work together, it’s impactful. We encourage you to join us in delivering essential services and programs to our diverse community. You won't find a better opportunity than Peel Region.

Additional Information

Peel Region is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace where everyone is respected and valued for their contributions, and where everyone is treated fairly and has opportunity to grow and develop. As one of the most diverse regions in Canada, we are committed to establishing a qualified workforce that is reflective of the population we serve.

Peel Region is committed to providing accommodations throughout the recruitment process, upon request. If you require accommodation, please notify us and we will work with you to meet your needs. Accessible formats and communication supports are available. Please contact zzg-hrtalentacquisition@peelregion.ca

Please be advised, Peel Region uses email to communicate with applicants for open job competitions and does not use AI technology in any part of the recruitment process. It is the applicant’s responsibility to include an updated email address that is checked daily and accepts emails from unknown users. As we send time sensitive correspondence via email (i.e., testing bookings, interview dates), it is imperative that applicants check their email regularly. If we do not hear back from applicants, we will assume that you are no longer interested in the position and your application will be removed from the competition.

jobs.description:

About Us

At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Income Assistance (IA), Supportive Housing and Homelessness, and the Disability Support Program (DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong, dedicated network of supports and staff to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity

Financial leadership in OSD has a direct connection to the programs, services and external providers that support Nova Scotians. As Director of Finance, you will lead a complex, province-wide financial operation and help ensure that leaders have the accurate information, practical advice and effective controls needed to make responsible decisions.

This is an opportunity to combine professional accounting expertise with broader leadership. You will guide financial operations, strengthen planning and risk management, support sound decision-making, and lead a sizeable team through competing priorities and organizational change. Your success will depend not only on technical knowledge, but also on your judgement, communication, relationship-building, and ability to help others deliver results.

Primary Accountabilities

In this role, you have the opportunity to lead a substantial finance function, advise senior decision-makers and improve the systems and practices that support programs and services across Nova Scotia. A few of your key responsibilities are to:

Provide strategic and operational financial advice to the Executive Director and senior leaders, translating complex financial and non-financial information into clear options, risks and recommendations.
Lead the delivery and continuous improvement of financial operations that support departmental programs, regional teams and external service providers.
Provide leadership for budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis and the management of cost pressures, helping leaders make informed choices about resources and program delivery.
Strengthen financial accountability through effective internal controls, risk management, transparent reporting and compliance with applicable accounting standards and government financial policies.
Lead, support and develop a geographically distributed finance team. Set clear direction, build management capability, encourage collaboration and create the conditions for people to take ownership of their work.
Provide clear direction and leadership to managers and staff by establishing priorities, clarifying accountabilities, delegating effectively and supporting consistent delivery across the finance function.
Build the capability and resilience of the finance team through workforce planning, coaching, performance management and succession development.
Exercise sound professional judgment and critical thinking in interpreting and applying provincial government financial policies and applicable accounting standards within complex and diverse contexts, considering both financial and non-financial information.
Build productive relationships across OSD and with central agencies, internal audit, legal partners, service providers and other stakeholders. Address difficult issues with diplomacy while maintaining professional standards and public accountability.
Lead practical improvements to financial processes, systems and service delivery. Sequence change thoughtfully so that essential operations remain stable and responsive.
Represent the department on relevant cross-government initiatives, committees and working groups, and communicate financial issues clearly to both financial and non-financial audiences.

Qualifications And Experience

You are a designated Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) with progressively responsible experience leading financial operations and people in a complex organization. Your experience demonstrates that you can:

lead managers and professional staff in a complex work environment, including setting expectations, delegating responsibility, developing capability and addressing performance concerns.
assess workforce and organizational needs, strengthen team capacity and guide employees through operational or organizational change while maintaining service delivery.
prepare and deliver briefings or presentations for executive-level audiences, including providing credible financial advice and explaining complex issues
support budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis and the management of significant or competing financial pressures;
establish or strengthen internal controls, accountability and risk-management practices;
build effective relationships and resolve difficult issues with sound judgement, discretion and diplomacy; and
organize work, adapt to changing priorities and deliver accurate advice within tight timeframes.

You bring a practical understanding of professional accounting standards and the ability to apply financial policy in a complex operating environment. You also understand that strong financial management requires attention to program and service outcomes, not only financial results.

The Following Experience Would Be Considered An Asset

audit, assurance or control-review work;
public-sector, human-services, not-for-profit or other complex service-delivery finance;
financial relationships with funded organizations, service providers, grants or contribution agreements;
Public Sector Accounting Standards and government financial policy

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency

We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits

Based on the employment status, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short- and Long-Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions

Your typical work week is 35 hours with 7-hour days. The role includes regular travel to regional offices and other work sites across Nova Scotia.

Additional Information

An offer of employment is conditional upon satisfactory completion of all applicable background checks and confirmation of credentials, including: Education Verification and Criminal Background Check.

What We Offer

Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career
Engaging workplace: our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies
Countless career paths

jobs.title: Director, Equipment Planning and Biomedical Services
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Director, Equipment Planning and Biomedical Services is accountable for clinical and non-clinical asset planning, maintenance and management. The role provides overall leadership to Mackenzie Health equipment needs for short-term and long-term asset planning, tracking, maintenance, management, and refresh. The director is responsible for overseeing all facility and redevelopment work required to plan, procure, and complete installation of medical equipment. This role also provides Director-level leadership to the Central Equipment and Biomedical Engineering departments. This role works within an environment that has Design-Build-Finance-Maintain (DBFP) equipment relationships, Managed Equipment Services (MES) contract, as well as a traditional in-house biomedical engineering service and support model. This role also works closely with Mackenzie Health Redevelopment department to plan, procure, and implement the Furniture, Fixtures, and Equipment (FF&E) components of various redevelopment projects. Additionally, the Director coordinates efforts with various departments to develop and maintain a multi-year equipment plan and budget, ensuring appropriate inventory levels, mitigation of corporate risk, and balances demand with broader organizational need.

Primary Responsibilities

Maintain current knowledge of laws, ordinances, and regulations pertaining to corporate purchasing practices.
Working in close collaboration with corporate procurement, develop a multi year clinical technology strategy, in conjunction with clinical and nonclinical leaders, and that aligns with organizational priorities. The strategy must include centralized purchasing/procurement of materials, equipment, machinery, and services required for operations, projects, and capital investments.
Responsible for the implementation of all Equipment projects from needs identification through to commissioning and on-going maintenance.
Manage and oversee all aspects of large-scale equipment installation projects including managing internal and external stakeholders, shop drawing reviews, scope of work development, project schedule development, budget management, reporting, commissioning, training, and close-out documentation.
Work collaboratively with the Digital Health portfolio to ensure all required integrations are planned and implemented to support equipment use.
Provide executive leadership with strategic and tactical advice, as well as risks and opportunities related to emerging healthcare technologies and long-term organizational planning.
Provide advice to management at all levels by using knowledge of equipment market and procurement.
Working in close collaboration with corporate procurement, supervise or manage complex negotiations to settle commercial disputes and claims with suppliers by establishing goals and approving commercial settlements.
Manage the Philips MESP contract ($300M+ over 14-year contract life) and provide support to Philips and the Mackenzie Clinical team in the administration of the MESP contracted services.
Provide direct leadership to Biomedical Engineering and Central Equipment staff and services across a multi site hospital system.
Establish policies and procedures supporting safe equipment use and maintenance.
Lead service contract procurement and negotiations.
Monitor vendor performance and service level agreements.
Develop performance KPI for adequate service and support of medical equipment.
Work with multiple equipment vendors to coordinate design and construction activities, monitor performance and intervene to rectify issues.
Ensure the development and maintenance of work systems, goals and objectives, management systems, teamwork, and resource management for departments within the area of accountability.
Create and maintain asset management and tracking workflows and processes.
Create and maintain a space management program.
Space management includes oversight and recommendations to resolve all space requests. Working collaboratively with Redevelopment, Facilities, Clinical, Clinical Support Teams to ensure space allocations are prioritized and allocated based on hospital priorities.
Act as Chair of the Change Request Group (SAFES) to ensure alignment with corporate vision and mission.
Manage the intake, review, and implementation of all changes related to Space, Aesthetics, Furniture, Equipment, and Signage.
Provide leadership, support, and direction to program staff on issues related to performance, corporate direction, service delivery, staff development, Human Resources Management (HRM), realignment, and change management strategies.
Direct the process of establishing, implementing, and reporting on appropriate quality and productivity indicator measurement tools, based on provincial benchmarks, best practice standards, and legislative requirements.
Co-develop annual budgets and operating plans that align with the hospital’s programs and directives, and ensure the program stays within budget.
Ensure all assigned employees comply with hospital, government, and customer policies, procedures, and regulations.
Build external and internal business relationships to gather information, identify market and industry trends, build partnership and alliances to support and facilitate the hospital’s objectives and plans.
Management of Regulatory Requirements as applicable to equipment installations ensuring all documentation is submitted and approved by appropriate regulatory bodies to support the installation and use of medical equipment (e.g. HARP, CNSC).
Ensure effective procurement activities that meet the requirements and needs of the hospital’s internal stakeholders.
Ensure a safe environment for patients, staff, and visitors; investigate, report, debrief and take or direct corrective action as appropriate on incidents.
Manage human resources which include recruitment, selection and training.
Teach, coach and lead staff in the development and monitoring of quality indicators and improvement initiatives.
Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders/organizations/community groups to achieve program objectives, integrate, and link services and foster partnerships across the continuum of service delivery.
Participate in education and training specific to current, relevant federal and provincial health and safety legislation, standards, and guidelines.

What must you have?

Minimum of a Master’s Degree or Master’s ready in Business, Economics, or in a related field, from an accredited university.
Minimum of 5-10 years experience working in equipment planning and procurement within a health care environment.
Minimum of five (5) years’ working in a senior leadership role, preferably in a health care environment.
Biomedical service leadership experience is required or similar experience that is deemed equivalent.
Training or recent experience with drafting requests for proposals and vendor agreements is required.

What else do you bring?

Strong knowledge of hospital operations.
Demonstrated experience in negotiating and managing large, complex contracts.
Demonstrated knowledge of the appropriate tools for grading, analyzing, and assessing materials, equipment, supplies, services, and other commodities.
Demonstrated knowledge of Supply Chain Management (SCM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Material Requirements Planning (MRP) software.
Demonstrated excellent critical and logical thinking, analysis, and reasoning to identify underlying principles, reasons, or facts.
Demonstrated project management, change management, and analytical thinking skills.
Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, and influence individuals and teams toward a vision, while maintaining group cohesiveness and effectiveness.
Demonstrated strategic business sense with financial management and budget development skills.
Demonstrated understanding of interrelationships between clinical and support programs.
Demonstrated ability to manage complex systems and human resources at the executive level.
Demonstrated leadership skills with ability to foster relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to coach, advise and teach others using the principles of adult learning.
Demonstrated training, experience, or utilization of lean methodology for process improvement.
Demonstrated ability to independently identify issues, plan improvements, measure success and continue improvement.
Proven attendance record.
Demonstrates understanding and complies with patient and staff safety policies and procedures that foster a safe and inclusive environment for all.
Ability to perform the essential duties of the job.
Effectively uses empathy in interactions with others.
Demonstrates behaviours consistent with Mackenzie Health’s Commitment to Caring.
Models behaviour that is aligned with the values of Mackenzie Health – Excellence, Leadership and Empathy.
Commitment to providing an exceptional experience for staff and clients within a challenging and exciting health care environment.

Preferably, Your Profile Also Includes

Additional specialized training will be considered an asset (e.g. Professional Certification in Supply Chain Logistics (P. Log) or a Designation as a Supply Chain Management Professional (SCMP).
You may be required to work at any site of Mackenzie Health.

Mackenzie Health is an inclusive and equal opportunity employer committed to providing accommodations for applicants upon request at any stage of the recruitment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and the Ontario Human Rights Code.

jobs.title: Director, Information Security, Ongoing Monitoring
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You’ll Be Doing

The Third-Party Risk Management team helps CIBC manage supplier risk across the enterprise by providing oversight, governance, and ongoing monitoring of third-party relationships. As a Director, Information Security, Ongoing Monitoring, you’ll lead a team responsible for building and delivering capabilities that monitor the risk profile of CIBC’s existing supplier relationships on an ongoing basis. You’ll work closely with third-party risk management lifecycle partners and key stakeholders, including pre-contract due diligence teams, control groups, and vendor relationship managers, to help ensure supplier risk remains within CIBC’s risk tolerance. In this senior leadership role, you’ll define and execute a risk-based supplier monitoring program that aligns with CIBC policy and global regulatory requirements, while supporting consistent governance across lines of business. You’ll also act as a key advisor on supplier risk, remediation, regulatory matters, and program improvements, while coaching and developing your team.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You’ll Succeed

Lead ongoing monitoring – Define and deliver a risk-based ongoing supplier risk monitoring program that aligns with CIBC policies, regulatory requirements, and enterprise risk tolerance. Maintain supporting processes and procedure documentation to ensure consistency and effectiveness.
Strengthen enterprise governance – Partner with lines of business and vendor relationship managers to support appropriate governance and oversight of third-party services. Provide direction and operational support to help teams effectively manage supplier relationships and monitor contract adherence.
Maintain supplier risk insights – Oversee supplier risk profiles across the enterprise and maintain a global risk tiering approach for suppliers and arrangements. Use internal, external, and supplier information sources to identify areas of exposure and determine the appropriate monitoring model for each tier.
Support remediation and regulatory readiness – Execute supplier risk assessments, partner with business units to develop remediation plans, and track issues through to resolution. Act as a point of contact for control testing, audit activity, and regulatory inquiries related to ongoing monitoring.
Enable global program maturity – Keep current on applicable global regulations and ensure regional and subsidiary needs are reflected in the program. Work to harmonize regulatory expectations into a consistent enterprise approach and continuously improve the program based on industry trends and business needs.
Lead and develop a high-performing team – Provide leadership, coaching, and mentorship to team members while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing environment aligned to CIBC’s purpose, vision, and values.

Who You Are

You can demonstrate 5 years of experience in third-party risk management, supplier risk monitoring, information security oversight, vendor governance, and working within a large, regulated environment. You have knowledge of risk management practices, supplier evaluation, and the broader information technology environment. It’s an asset if you have experience interpreting global third-party risk regulations and working across multiple jurisdictions.
You are a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing and implementing strategic team goals. You have experience coaching employees and inspiring successful team performance.
Your influence makes a difference. You know that relationships and networks are essential to success. You inspire outcomes by sharing your expertise.
You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complicated problems and making sense of information. You communicate detailed information in a meaningful way.
You act like an owner. You thrive when you're empowered to take initiative, go above and beyond, and deliver results.
You look beyond the moment. You know what you do will make a difference today and tomorrow. You look for new opportunities to define what’s possible.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

What You Need To Know

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com
CIBC is committed to clarity in our hiring process. All roles posted are opportunities we’re actively recruiting for, unless stated otherwise.
You need to be legally eligible to work at the location(s) specified above and, where applicable, must have a valid work or study permit.
We may ask you to complete an attribute-based assessment and other skills test (such as simulation, coding, French proficiency).
We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

new_jobs.title: Director, Information Security, Ongoing Monitoring
new_jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You’ll Be Doing

The Third-Party Risk Management team helps CIBC manage supplier risk across the enterprise by providing oversight, governance, and ongoing monitoring of third-party relationships. As a Director, Information Security, Ongoing Monitoring, you’ll lead a team responsible for building and delivering capabilities that monitor the risk profile of CIBC’s existing supplier relationships on an ongoing basis. You’ll work closely with third-party risk management lifecycle partners and key stakeholders, including pre-contract due diligence teams, control groups, and vendor relationship managers, to help ensure supplier risk remains within CIBC’s risk tolerance. In this senior leadership role, you’ll define and execute a risk-based supplier monitoring program that aligns with CIBC policy and global regulatory requirements, while supporting consistent governance across lines of business. You’ll also act as a key advisor on supplier risk, remediation, regulatory matters, and program improvements, while coaching and developing your team.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You’ll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you’ll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You’ll Succeed

Lead ongoing monitoring – Define and deliver a risk-based ongoing supplier risk monitoring program that aligns with CIBC policies, regulatory requirements, and enterprise risk tolerance. Maintain supporting processes and procedure documentation to ensure consistency and effectiveness.
Strengthen enterprise governance – Partner with lines of business and vendor relationship managers to support appropriate governance and oversight of third-party services. Provide direction and operational support to help teams effectively manage supplier relationships and monitor contract adherence.
Maintain supplier risk insights – Oversee supplier risk profiles across the enterprise and maintain a global risk tiering approach for suppliers and arrangements. Use internal, external, and supplier information sources to identify areas of exposure and determine the appropriate monitoring model for each tier.
Support remediation and regulatory readiness – Execute supplier risk assessments, partner with business units to develop remediation plans, and track issues through to resolution. Act as a point of contact for control testing, audit activity, and regulatory inquiries related to ongoing monitoring.
Enable global program maturity – Keep current on applicable global regulations and ensure regional and subsidiary needs are reflected in the program. Work to harmonize regulatory expectations into a consistent enterprise approach and continuously improve the program based on industry trends and business needs.
Lead and develop a high-performing team – Provide leadership, coaching, and mentorship to team members while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing environment aligned to CIBC’s purpose, vision, and values.

Who You Are

You can demonstrate 5 years of experience in third-party risk management, supplier risk monitoring, information security oversight, vendor governance, and working within a large, regulated environment. You have knowledge of risk management practices, supplier evaluation, and the broader information technology environment. It’s an asset if you have experience interpreting global third-party risk regulations and working across multiple jurisdictions.
You are a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing and implementing strategic team goals. You have experience coaching employees and inspiring successful team performance.
Your influence makes a difference. You know that relationships and networks are essential to success. You inspire outcomes by sharing your expertise.
You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complicated problems and making sense of information. You communicate detailed information in a meaningful way.
You act like an owner. You thrive when you're empowered to take initiative, go above and beyond, and deliver results.
You look beyond the moment. You know what you do will make a difference today and tomorrow. You look for new opportunities to define what’s possible.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com

We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.
